title: Instrumentation slab + runways: metrics, spans, dashboards (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for creating an "instrumentation slab" concept and a lightweight runway for onboarding new models/features into our observability fabric. The goal: group instrumentation into a minimal cohesive slab that makes rollouts predictable for ops, reduces noise for oncall, and standardizes tracing handoffs so debug paths are obvious.

Context / motivation:
- We keep adding probes and panels per-feature and end up with inconsistent dashboards and trace anchors.
- Oncall frequently asks: "Which span tells me the model choice / fallback / cache hit?" and we don't have a reliable answer across services.
- Need an onboarding runway so new model rollouts include a minimal telemetry contract before traffic is ramped.

Key concepts (working definitions):
- Instrumentation slab: a bounded set of metrics, traces, and dashboard panels that are sufficient to operate a single inference surface (e.g., hosted API generation route) for day-1 rollouts. Think of it as the smallest slice needed for ops/readiness.
- Runway: the onboarding checklist and timeline (smoke probes, SLI probes, detailed spans) that must be satisfied before canary -> gradual rollout -> full release.
- Span family / handoff anchor: a named set of spans that must exist and be present in traces to anchor down stream token paths (model selection, routing, kv-cache, model-inference, postprocess).

Proposed slab contents (minimum):
1) Metrics (per-route and per-tenant when applicable):
   - request_count: counter (labels: route, tenant, model_variant, region)
       - definition: increment on every entry to inference routing.
   - ttf_token_ms_p50/p90/p99: histogram/summary (route, model_variant)
       - definition: time from request enqueue to first token produced (ms).
   - token_emitted_count: counter (route, model_variant)
       - definition: tokens emitted by runtime. Useful for cost attribution.
   - kv_cache_hit_ratio: gauge (route, tenant)
       - definition: ratio (hits / attempts) over sliding window.
   - fallback_rate: counter / ratio (route)
       - definition: times a fallback policy was triggered (model variant, region).
   - error_rate_5m: ratio (route, region)
       - definition: (non-2xx responses / total) over 5m window.
   - queue_backlog: gauge (worker_pool, pod)
       - definition: number of pending requests awaiting compute.
   - batching_efficiency: gauge (model_variant)
       - definition: avg tokens per batch / expected tokens per batch (heuristic).

2) Tracing (span naming and required attributes):
   - span: request.receive (root)
       - attrs: request.id, route, tenant.id, client.version
   - span: routing.select-model
       - attrs: model_catalog_id, model_variant, policy (latency|cost|region), decision_reason
   - span: cache.kv.lookup
       - attrs: cache_key, hit:boolean, kv_latency_ms
   - span: model.inference
       - attrs: model_variant, seq_len_requested, seq_len_returned, gpu_node_id(optional), quantized:boolean
   - span: postprocess.format
       - attrs: token_count, truncated:boolean
   - span: fallback.swap
       - attrs: from_variant, to_variant, latency_penalty_ms
   - Trace correlation: every span must include request.id and trace.parent when applicable.

   Sampling guidance (budgeted):
   - Adaptive sampling that ensures: 100% of errors; 10% of high-latency (p99) paths; and 1% base sampling of steady-state successes.
   - Tenant-weighted reserve: for high-priority tenants (enterprise) keep additional 0.5% sampling budget to support debug requests.

3) Dashboards (lane definitions):
   - Triage lane (operator quick-check): 6 panels showing request_count, error_rate_5m, ttf_token_ms_p99, kv_cache_hit_ratio, queue_backlog, and active_model_variant. Short TTL, colorized thresholds for fast f0.
   - Forensics lane (deeper): top 5 trace anchors, error breakdown by model_variant, fallback_rate timeline, per-tenant token_emitted_cost estimate, and heatmap of token latencies by seq_len.
   - Cost lane: tokens emitted per route * cost/unit by model_variant, batching_efficiency trend, and cost per 1k tokens over last 24h.

Runway / onboarding checklist (minimal):
- Pre-canary (developer): define slab contract in PR (list of metrics + spans + dashboard wireframe). Link: JIRA ticket.
- Canary readiness: smoke probe (synthetic probe) that hits the route and asserts response correctness and ttf_token_ms_p90 < target.
- Tracing: traces for synthetic probe must include span family and show cache hits/misses.
- Dashboards: triage lane created and linked in PR, default owner assigned.
- Alerting: temporary warn-only alerts for error_rate_5m and p99 latency.
- Rollout gate: only allow >10% traffic after canary probes pass for 1 hour and no sustained SLO violations.

Dashboards / panel design rules (opinions):
- One concept per panel: avoid mixing cost + latency in same tiny panel.
- Use quantile lines for latency panels, stacked bars for token counts by variant.
- Panels should clearly show "model variant run-up" when rollouts happen (annotate with deployments).
- Add a compact trace link column that includes top span timings (cached, routing, model).

Ownership and Stewardship:
- Owner: feature team (first owner) + observability as platform curator. Feature team must declare a 30-day post-launch steward.
- Metric steward responsibilities: ensure metric semantics, migration notes, and deprecation window.
- Dashboard stewards: minimize panels (<=10) for triage lane, maintain annotations for rollouts.

Investigation playbook (compact):
1) Look at triage lane: is error_rate_5m elevated? Is p99 token TTF elevated?
2) If error spike: open traces with sampling filter (errors 100%). Find first failing span (routing/model/cache).
3) If latency spike with high queue_backlog: suspect scale / autoscaler tuning. Check batch sizes.
4) If fallbacks increased: check routing.select-model span attributes to see reasons.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Metric cardinality: how far do we carry tenant/model_variant labels before explosion? Proposal: route+model_variant+region only for high-volume metrics; tenant only for cost and dedicated SLOs. (Decide via cost simulation.)
- How do we instrument quantization metadata without a heavy label set? Suggest embedding quantized:boolean as span attr (trace) not metric label.
- Sampling config: need central policy and feature flags to change sampling per-tenant.
- Hooking structured logs into traces: quick wins vs long-term work.

Next 30d plan (practical steps):
- Week 1: align with serving-runtime and platform-engineering on span names and required attrs. (owners: Marco + Leah).
- Week 2: add slab contract checklist to the release checklist template. Create PR template that enforces slab metadata. (owner: Aisha).
- Week 3: implement synthetic probe template (small harness) and add to probes repo. (owner: Devon).
- Week 4: pilot with 1 route (hosted/api/generation) and iterate. Capture lessons and refine runways.

Appendix: quick examples
- Example metric name: inference.requests.count{route="/v1/generate",model_variant="redwood-xl-8k",region="us-west-2"}
- Example span tags: {request.id: "r_123", model_variant: "redwood-xl-8k", kv_hit: true}

Notes to self / friction log:
- Keep the slab small. Ops fatigue is real.
- Avoid adding expensive cardinality labels to high-frequency metrics. Use traces for cardinality.
- Make rollout annotations easy to emit from release-engineering pipeline.

If you have time: please add notes on alert thresholds we should carry (p95 TTF, p99 TTF, error_rate_5m, kv_cache_hit_ratio) with suggested numeric thresholds for low/medium/high severity based on route SLA.

-- end working sketch --
